correctness.rationale: At first arrival at frontier v_j, every earlier rotor points toward it. A departure into a subtree whose rotors all point back toward the frontier makes a full excursion, moving twice along every edge in that subtree including its attachment; this follows inductively because each child starts with its rotor pointing to its parent and the next parent exit follows a complete cycle through its children. All these excursions restore the parent-pointing orientations. Before the first exit to v_{j+1}, the 2j+1 edges of the prefix tree can contribute at most 4j+2 traversals; equality uses every prefix branch and requires the untouched frontier rotor initially to point to v_{j+1}. The final exit contributes one step and puts the prefix in the same rooted form for the induction. A periodic state on the tree must be a unicycle with the chip on its cycle: over a period every vertex visited uses all its exits and thus every vertex is visited, and last-departure times strictly increase along last-exit arrows away from any nonchip vertex unless the next vertex is the terminal chip position. Conversely, removing the chip rotor from a unicycle gives rotors directed toward the chip; a full root tour restores the state. First arrival at v_{n−1} always satisfies this criterion, and summing 4j+3 gives the bound. With terminal rotor pointing to its leaf that off-chip dimer prevents earlier recurrence. With terminal rotor left and all others forward, recurrence already occurs at first arrival to v_{n−2}, including at time zero for n=2. Hence the maximizer is unique.
residual_risks: The exhaustive check is finite; the induction and recurrence proof establish all n. The result fixes the starting endpoint and the specified orders.

evidence: Chalopin et al. give the previously known general bound 2mD, here 2(2n−1)(n+1). Poghosyan–Priezzhev characterize recurrent unicycles.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The general bound has a larger leading coefficient and gives no equality case; a criterion at an already reached state is not an exact time to reach it.

value.rationale: The comb is a natural next family beyond paths and a standard rotor-routing graph. The exact clock gives a benchmark for quadratic transients at an endpoint, quantifies the effect of the private leaves beyond a generic order bound, and identifies which terminal cycle delays periodic entry. The maximizer is not determined by the general recurrence characterization.
residual_risks: Not a maximum over starts, rotor orders, or trees, and no distribution of submaximal transients is asserted.
